content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in the short term, showing a lag in adjusting to true market sentiment.", "Sentiment indicators with positive values correlate with higher forecasted prices, but do not reliably predict sharp reversals.", "True outcomes often exhibit mean-reversion after initial peaks, especially when sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral or bearish.", "Models fail to capture early bearish sentiment signals, leading to delayed price corrections and persistent overestimation.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment history shows sustained negative bias, indicating model calibration is needed for downward trends.", "Price drops are frequently underestimated by models, especially when sentiment turns negative within the last 5-7 days.", "Models show diminishing predictive power when sentiment is volatile or mixed, suggesting a need for sentiment-weighted smoothing.", "Forecast bias is most pronounced in the first 10 days of the 30-day window, indicating a need for dynamic adjustment based on recent sentiment shifts."]}
